title: Quasi-fundamental domain from a closed alcove (App B)
body_html:
Quasi-fundamental domain from a closed alcove

Setting (following [Kaletha–Prasad]): Let $G$ be reductive over a $p$-adic field $F$, $F^{\mathrm{ur}}$ its unramified closure, $G^1(F) := G^1(F^{\mathrm{ur}}) \cap G(F)$ (kernel of all unramified characters), $G^0(F)$ the kernel of the Kottwitz map. Let $T \subseteq G$ be a maximal $F$-split torus, $N := N(G, T)$, $N^0 := N \cap G^0(F)$, $A = X_*(T) \otimes \mathbb{R}$ the apartment of the extended building, $A' = A / A(Z_G)$ the apartment of the reduced building.

Let $\mathcal{C}'$ be an alcove in $A'$, $\mathcal{C} := \mathrm{pr}^{-1}(\mathcal{C}') \subseteq A$. Let $N_{\mathcal{C}'}$ stabilize $\mathcal{C}'$ in $N$, $N^0_{\mathcal{C}'} = N_{\mathcal{C}'} \cap G(k)^0$.

Claim. $\mathcal{C}$ is a quasi-fundamental domain of the $N$-action on $A$, with stabilizing subgroup $N_{\mathcal{C}'}$.
proof_html:
$N_{\mathcal{C}'} / N^0_{\mathcal{C}'} \cong \Omega$ (the Kottwitz/abelian quotient). With $W = N / T(k)^0$ and $W^{\mathrm{aff}} = N^0 / T(k)^0$, $W = \Omega \ltimes W^{\mathrm{aff}}$.

Suppose $x, y \in \mathcal{C}$ with $nx = y$, $n \in N$. Write $n = ab$ with $a \in \Omega$, $b \in W^{\mathrm{aff}}$. Then $bx = a^{-1}y$. Since $\mathcal{C}'$ is a fundamental domain for $W^{\mathrm{aff}}$ on $A'$, $\mathrm{pr}(bx) = \mathrm{pr}(x)$ forces $bx = x$ on the reduced part, and $b$ fixes the $V(A_G)$ part, so $bx = x$ and $y = ax$ is in the $\Omega$-orbit of $x$. $\square$

Freeness on the free part of $\Omega$

Decompose $\Omega = \Omega_{\mathrm{free}} \times \Omega_{\mathrm{tor}}$ with $\Omega_{\mathrm{free}}$ free abelian.

Lemma. $\Omega_{\mathrm{free}}$ acts freely on $\mathcal{C}$.

Proof. Any $n \in N_\Omega$ fixing a point of the extended building lies in $N_\Omega \cap G^1(k)$, i.e. the torsion part. $\square$

This is the geometric foundation for the unramified-character / $\hat K_{x_0}$ cocycle construction in [[node:depth_zero_reduction.E2_construction]].
